title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review findings on PR #524 head 7199f7a
description:
Supervisor's OWN fresh review of head 7199f7a (PR #524), run per the standing instruction to self-review after clearing a reviewer's findings and loop until clean. Review #5097921608's single blocker is CONFIRMED FIXED: currentPosition is a required field on all three mutation APIs, checkTemporalMode rejects a prospective rule effective before the current position, and the bounded disputed-turn exception still works for the current and immediately preceding turn (verified by supervisor; the 6 new regressions fail against 7c8eafe).

TWO NEW BLOCKING DEFECTS, both reproduced by the supervisor at 7199f7a.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev4 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev4, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 7199f7a. Run `npm ci` first if node_modules is missing; verify:worktree now enforces worktree-local resolution.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — currentPosition is caller-asserted and never checked against real campaign chronology, so the history rewrite the last review demanded be fixed is still reachable.
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.2 (mutation boundary), with eshyra-jhpt.3 owning the chronology source.
=============================================================
Making currentPosition a required ARGUMENT closed the "omitted authority" hole but not the "false authority" one. The store never consults campaign_turn_position, which is the campaign's real canonical chronology and lives in the same database. A caller that asserts a stale position backdates exactly as before.

REPRODUCED at 7199f7a — the campaign genuinely advanced to ordinal 10 through ten real resolveCampaignPosition calls, then:
    claimed currentPosition: 2  (real: 10)
    historical active-at-position(P5) now reports: [ 'backdated-via-stale-authority' ]   <- history rewritten again
This is the same defect the previous review blocked on, one level down: the parameter is now mandatory but unverified.

FIX: make the campaign's current canonical position authoritative from persisted state rather than from the caller.
  - Add a read-only accessor alongside resolveCampaignPosition (campaign/campaignPosition.ts) that returns the campaign's current canonical position without allocating one — the MAX-ordinal row for that campaign. resolveCampaignPosition must stay as-is; it ASSIGNS, and moving it would break the turn lifecycle and .8's replay reuse.
  - Then either (a) drop the currentPosition parameter from the three mutation APIs and resolve it internally, or (b) keep the parameter and reject it when it disagrees with the persisted current position. (a) is simpler and cannot be bypassed; (b) keeps callers explicit. Choose one, state why, and make the other impossible rather than merely discouraged.
  - Define and test the behaviour for a campaign with NO turn positions yet (a brand-new campaign creating its first rule). Do not let that case silently permit arbitrary backdating.
EVIDENCE: advance real chronology to ordinal 10 via resolveCampaignPosition, then prove a mutation asserting an earlier current position is rejected (or ignored in favour of the persisted value) for create, revoke and supersede, and that historical active-at-position results are unchanged. Must fail against 7199f7a.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking) — two channels carry current-position authority and they contradict each other; supplying both rejects a legitimate supersession.
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.1 / eshyra-jhpt.2.
=============================================================
SupersedeCampaignRuleInput now has BOTH `currentPosition` (required) and `validation.currentPosition` (optional, pre-existing). supersedeCampaignRule deliberately validates the historical prior rule with `input.validation` alone — correct, because the prior is legitimately older than the current position — but a caller that also sets validation.currentPosition causes that same prior to be validated against it and rejected.

REPRODUCED at 7199f7a, stating the same truth through both channels:
    supersede old(P1) -> new(P10), currentPosition: P10, validation: { currentPosition: P10 }
    -> "prospective campaign rule cannot take effect before the current position"
A correct, non-adversarial call fails. The prior rule is historical by definition; validating it against "now" is never right.

FIX: one authority for current position. Preferred: remove currentPosition from CampaignRuleValidationOptions entirely (or stop threading caller-supplied validation into the prior-rule check) so the historical prior can never be evaluated against the current position, and the mutation APIs' own current-position field is the single source. If CampaignRuleValidationOptions.currentPosition must stay for the disputed-turn path, make it structurally impossible for it to reach the prior-rule validation, and document which check owns which rule.
EVIDENCE: a test that supersedes an old prospective rule while supplying current-position authority through every channel the API exposes, and succeeds. Plus the existing disputed-turn coverage must keep passing.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 7199f7a; report observed counts, do not infer them.
  - Do not weaken existing tests. Updating call sites for a changed signature is expected; relaxing an assertion is not.
  - Do not touch the four fixes from review #5097622281, the position encoding, the seam contract, merged migrations, or the active-at-position predicate.
  - Keep the bounded disputed-turn exception working for the current and immediately preceding turn.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolves into this worktree.

=============================================================
ADDITIONAL FINDINGS from a supplementary /code-review sweep of the branch (supervisor triaged each; these six are accepted, one was rejected).
=============================================================

FINDING 3 (blocking) — checkTemporalMode's `sameTurn` ignores ordinal, so a disputed-turn rule can be backdated arbitrarily far.
campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode accepts a disputed-turn rule when disputedPosition.sessionId/turnId equal currentPosition's, WITHOUT comparing ordinals — while the sibling `immediatelyBefore` branch does compare them. Ordinal is the documented authoritative chronology field.
Reproduced by the sweep: currentPosition { s1, 't-current', ordinal 100 } with effectivePosition = disputedPosition = { s1, 't-current', ordinal 3 } is ACCEPTED, and listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition at ordinal 50 returns the rule — a house rule silently backdated across 97 resolved positions, exactly what revoke/supersede now refuse.
FIX: require disputedPosition.ordinal === currentPosition.ordinal in the sameTurn branch. Note this interacts with FINDING 1: a legitimately resolved (session, turn) pair has exactly one ordinal because campaign_turn_position is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id), so this only becomes reachable through a caller-fabricated position — which is precisely what FINDING 1 is about. Fix both; neither alone is sufficient.

FINDING 4 — createCampaignRule leaks a raw SqliteError on duplicate identity.
campaignRuleStore.ts createCampaignRule has no duplicate-identity guard and relies on PRIMARY KEY (campaign_id, rule_identity). Creating the same identity twice throws SqliteError "UNIQUE constraint failed", and `e instanceof CampaignRuleError` is false — while supersedeCampaignRule explicitly guards the analogous case with "campaign rule 'X' already exists". A caller catching CampaignRuleError to turn a bad player request into a message instead gets an unhandled DB error naming SQL columns.
FIX: guard it like supersede does, throwing CampaignRuleError. Test it.

FINDING 5 — unvalidated pack JSON is cast to RulesAmbiguity and dereferenced at render time.
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack accepts any object with a string `id` (`value as RulesAmbiguity`) and checks nothing else; contextAssembler.ts renderContextMessage then reads ambiguity.question and calls ambiguity.interpretations.map(...). Supervisor confirmed this is REACHABLE, not merely defensive: pack-load validation of mechanics.ambiguities via optRulesAmbiguities is applied per record KIND, and the kind schemas do not cover all 15 RULES_RECORD_KINDS, while the pack-level assertAmbiguityIdentityAndProvenance only touches `id` and `source`. So an ambiguity with a valid id and source but a missing or non-array `interpretations`, on a kind whose schema omits mechanics validation, passes pack load and then throws TypeError inside prompt rendering — failing EVERY turn for that campaign, far from the cause. A third-party/add-on pack supplied through CampaignRulesPackResolver is the realistic vector.
FIX: validate the ambiguity shape in ambiguitiesFromStack and either drop the entry or fail loudly there, with the record key in the message. Do not fix this at render time.

FINDING 6 — an active ambiguity ruling is rendered twice, with two different framings.
The discovery seam excludes ambiguity rulings from activeRulesAtPosition (!isAmbiguityRuling), but assembleCampaignRulesContext builds `rules` from listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition, which does not. The DM prompt therefore shows the same decision once in the rules list as "- [ruling] <id> (ambiguity:X#int-1; ...): <prose>" and again under its ambiguity as "Active ruling <id> (int-1): <prose>".
FIX: make the two consumers agree. The ambiguity subsection is the meaningful placement (it pairs the ruling with the source material it resolves, which is the point of amendment A1), so prefer excluding ambiguity rulings from the flat rules list. Assert the rendered output contains each ruling exactly once.

FINDING 7 — an ambiguity ruling cannot surface its own governing record, contradicting the seam's documented contract.
Because activeRulesAtPosition excludes ambiguity rulings, the only route to joinCampaignRules is activeRulingsForAmbiguities(ambiguityIds), and those ids are derived solely from ambiguities already present on candidate records. A ruling with governingRecordKeys ['spell:fireball'] resolving an ambiguity that spell:fireball does not itself carry is never returned, never placed, and never surfaces its governing record — while campaignRuleSeam.ts's own comment states "A governing record that resolves in the active stack therefore ENTERS as a candidate here." No unplaced-rule loss is recorded either, because the projection is never returned at all.
FIX: close the gap so an active ambiguity ruling reaches the join regardless of whether its ambiguity was already discovered, without reintroducing double-processing (the seam concatenates [...rules, ...rulings], so the same identity must not arrive twice) and without breaking FINDING 6's single-placement rule. If you conclude the correct answer is that the loss must at least be RECORDED rather than the ruling surfaced, argue it in your notes — but silence is not acceptable either way.

FINDING 8 (hardening, latent) — two different orderings are defined over the same value.
activeRows compares effective_position as SQLite BINARY text; compareCampaignPositions compares the DECODED sessionId/turnId. encodeURIComponent reorders: raw 'a b' < 'a!c' (0x20 < 0x21) but encoded 'a%20b' > 'a!c' (0x25 > 0x21). The zero-padded ordinal prefix masks this for any pair produced by resolveCampaignPosition, and UNIQUE (campaign_id, ordinal) makes equal-ordinal pairs impossible, so it is not reachable today — but these are the SQL predicate and the JS admission check for the same fact.
FIX: pin it. A shared canonical comparison is best; a comment at both sites naming the invariant that keeps them agreeing is the minimum. Do not restructure the encoding.

REJECTED FINDING (do not act on it): the sweep also flagged that every active rule and every stack ambiguity is injected into every turn. That is the deliberate contract of eshyra-jhpt.3 ("correctness takes priority over selective retrieval"; prompt retrieval optimization is an explicit non-goal), and the supervisor measured the per-turn scan at ~0.13 ms over 1812 records. It is recorded as eshyra-umyb for when pack curation or campaign age makes it material. Do not add relevance selection or truncation here.

Added getCurrentCampaignPosition (MAX ordinal) and mutation-boundary validation against persisted chronology, with explicit ordinal-zero behavior for campaigns with no turn positions. Removed validation.currentPosition as a mutation-validation channel; currentPosition is now the sole mutation authority. Same-turn disputed rules require matching ordinal. Duplicate creation maps to CampaignRuleError. Ambiguity pack data is validated at campaign-context assembly with the record key in failures. Ambiguity rulings are excluded from the flat DM rules list, discovered independently of prior ambiguity candidates, and deduplicated within and across discovery join passes. Documented the canonical-position SQL/decoded comparator invariant at both sites.
- Added regression coverage for stale create/revoke/supersede authority and unchanged historical active sets, no-position bootstrap, dual-channel supersession, same-turn ordinal backdating, duplicate identity, malformed ambiguity payloads, single rendered ruling placement, independent governing-record surfacing, and encoded-anchor ordering.
- Negative proof against 7199f7a: 3 files / 60 tests observed 8 failures and 52 passes (campaignRules 1, campaignRuleStore 5, contextAssembler 2). The latent F8 ordering invariant is not behaviorally reachable under canonical ordinal-first encoding and unique campaign ordinals; its invariant test passed on the base as expected.
- Required verification from this worktree passed: 276 test files passed / 3 skipped; 4868 tests passed / 20 skipped; hidden-Unicode, Biome check/format/lint, forced typecheck, and worktree-local @eshyra/core resolution passed. Existing Biome schema mismatch emitted one info diagnostic only.
